items.title: [field] Sync filled state after native form reset

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Fixes #5765.

Sync `Field.Control` and `Input` filled state with the native value after form reset. Covers nonempty defaults, canceled resets, external forms, controlled values, and an input replaced by a reset handler without emitting `onValueChange`.

Validation passed: related jsdom tests (1,145), Field/Input/Form browser tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (342 per engine), `pnpm typescript`, `pnpm eslint`, `pnpm stylelint`, and `pnpm prettier`. The reset regression tests fail on the unchanged base.

items.title: [fieldset] Keep the legend association in server-rendered markup

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Fieldset.Legend registered its id in a layout effect, so the server never saw it: Fieldset.Root (and a RadioGroup rendered through it) shipped without aria-labelledby until hydration. Reserve the legend id in the root up front, let the legend adopt it until its own registration runs, and drop the reservation once registration has settled without a legend. Mirrors how LabelableProvider keeps Field.Label associated during SSR.

<!-- Thanks so much for your PR, your contribution is appreciated! ❤️ -->

- [x] I have followed (at least) the [PR section of the contributing guide](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/blob/HEAD/CONTRIBUTING.md#sending-a-pull-request).

Related to #5597 (the `aria-labelledby` half). #5712 covers the `tabindex` half, so this should not close the issue on its own.

Server-rendered `Fieldset.Root` now carries `aria-labelledby` pointing at its `Fieldset.Legend`, and a `RadioGroup` rendered through the fieldset gets the same. Before, `Fieldset.Legend` registered its id in a layout effect, which never runs on the server, so the fieldset (and the radiogroup) shipped with no accessible name until hydration.

## Changes

- `Fieldset.Root` reserves the legend id up front with `useBaseUiId()` and points `aria-labelledby` at it until legend registration has settled. Registration happens in the legend's layout effect; the root's own layout effect runs after it (child-first), so both updates land in the same render.
- `Fieldset.Legend` renders the root's reserved id until its own registration runs, then switches to its explicit `id` if one was given. An explicit `id` therefore reaches the DOM after hydration, which is the same trade-off `LabelableProvider` makes for the control id in #5457.
- A root that never gets a legend drops the reservation once registration settles, so nothing dangles after hydration.
- `RadioGroup` needed no change: it already reads `fieldsetContext.legendId`, which is now correct at render time.

## Tests

- `FieldsetLegend.test.tsx`: the two SSR tests that encoded the old behaviour are rewritten (`aria-labelledby` is present and matches the legend in server markup; the explicit id is deferred until hydration but the association is kept; the reservation is dropped after hydration when there is no legend).
- `RadioGroup.test.tsx`: the exact case from #5597, `Field.Root > Fieldset.Root render={<RadioGroup />} > Fieldset.Legend`, asserts `aria-labelledby` in the server markup and after hydration.

Verified the new tests fail without the source change and pass with it. Fieldset, field, checkbox, checkbox-group, form, radio and radio-group suites pass in Chromium; fieldset and radio-group pass in JSDOM.

One thing worth a maintainer's eye: during SSR a `Fieldset.Root` with no legend now points `aria-labelledby` at the reserved id until hydration removes it. That matches what `Field.Label` does with `for` during SSR, but if you would rather not carry that for the no-legend case I am happy to gate it differently.

items.title: [field] Keep pending validation when a control is disabled

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: A bug, but worse, it used to behave as expected.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Regression from #5449.

Disabling a field (`Field.Root`, `Field.Control`, or `Fieldset` `disabled`) unregisters its control, and since #5449 that unregister path cancelled any in-flight async `validate` result or pending debounced commit. A field disabled while a server check was pending came back neutral, and the error never showed until the next edit or submit. In 1.7.0 the pending result still published and appeared once the field was re-enabled.

## Changes

- Disabling now only removes the form registration. The control keeps source ownership and its pending validation, which publishes as before.
- Only the control's unmount cleanup passes the new `unmounted` flag, which clears ownership and cancels pending work. Replacement by a different control still cancels through the existing ownership-transfer branch.
- Keeping ownership while disabled matters: a disabled control that is later unmounted or swapped can still identify itself and drop its stale result, so it cannot land on the replacement control.
- Added regression tests for both sequences: disabled-then-re-enabled publishes the result, and disabled-then-replaced drops it.

items.title: [use-render][field][combobox] Restore constrained types in the API reference

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Improvements or additions to the documentation.

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: A bug, but worse, it used to behave as expected.

labels.name: PR: out-of-date
labels.description: The pull request has merge conflicts and can't be merged.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

labels.name: component: combobox
labels.description: Changes related to the combobox component.

items.body:
## Problem

Three regressions in the generated API reference, found while verifying the 1.8.0 diff against 1.7.0:

| Location | 1.7.0 | Today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field/types.md` — `Field.Error` `match` | `boolean \| 'valid' \| 'badInput' \| …` (11 keys) | `boolean \| unknown` |
| `use-render/types.md` — `defaultTagName` (×2) | full `IntrinsicElements` union | `unknown` |
| `combobox/types.md` — `createItems()` `data` | n/a (new API) | the internal `'Base UI: items passed to createItems() cannot have an \`items\` array property…'` diagnostic literal, rendered as an accepted value |

The source still declares `keyof ValidityState` and `keyof React.JSX.IntrinsicElements`. Readers could not discover which validity keys or tag names are accepted, and the `createItems` entry presented a compile-time error message as valid input while hiding the real flat-or-grouped signature.

The first two arrived with the dependency bump in #5248 (`typescript-api-extractor` beta.4 → beta.6, `internal-docs-infra` canary.26 → canary.35).

## Cause

**Not the extractor.** Probing `typescript-api-extractor@1.0.0-beta.6` directly on `FieldError.tsx` shows it resolves `keyof ValidityState` correctly, emitting both the authored syntax and the resolved union:

```json
{ "kind": "typeOperator", "operator": "keyof",
  "type": { "kind": "external", "typeName": { "name": "ValidityState" } },
  "resolvedType": { "kind": "union", "types": [ "\"badInput\"", "\"customError\"", … ] } }
```

beta.6 also added a `typeOperatorOutput: 'syntaxOnly'` option that names `keyof React.JSX.IntrinsicElements` in its own docs, so this node kind is deliberate.

**`@mui/internal-docs-infra` is what lost it.** `pipeline/loadServerTypesMeta/formatType.mjs` dispatches through ten kind guards (`isExternalType`, `isIntrinsicType`, `isUnionType`, …) and has no `typeOperator` case, so it reaches `return 'unknown'`. `grep -r typeOperator` across canary.38 returns zero hits. The real fix belongs there.

## Workaround

docs-infra honours a JSDoc `@type` override that short-circuits kind dispatch — already the convention in this repo for data attributes and CSS variables. It is threaded into both the props table (`format.mjs:367`) and the function-parameter table (`format.mjs:456`):

- **`match`** — restored byte-for-byte to its 1.7.0 output.
- **`createItems()` `data`** — now documents `readonly Item[] | readonly { items: readonly Item[] }[] | undefined`, the actual accepted shape. (An inline parameter JSDoc; note the value must be written without `{}` braces there, unlike the property form.)

**`defaultTagName` is not fixed by this PR.** It is rendered inside a raw `type useRenderParameters = {…}` block, and `formatType`'s object-property branch calls itself without forwarding `jsdocTags`, so the override cannot reach it. No source-level change helps either — any node of kind `typeOperator` hits the `unknown` fallback regardless of aliasing. The tag is added anyway: it surfaces the constraint in the emitted JSDoc, and it will start rendering as the type itself once docs-infra forwards those tags.

## Notes

- **No public API change.** The overrides restate exactly what the source declares; only JSDoc comments were touched in `packages/`.
- All three overrides should be **deleted** once docs-infra handles `typeOperator` (and forwards `jsdocTags` in the object-property branch), after which `pnpm docs:api` should reproduce the same output on its own.
- Gates: `pnpm typescript`, `pnpm eslint`, `pnpm prettier` all pass. `docs/` changes are `pnpm docs:api` output, not hand-edited.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: [field] Publish neutral validity while async validation is in flight

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: A bug, but worse, it used to behave as expected.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
While an async `validate` function is in flight, the field published `data-valid` (a fresh all-clear from native constraints) even though the result is unknown, and only `validationMode="onSubmit"` retired the previous result. It also dropped known native failures in that window, so a `required` or `type="email"` field could submit past its native constraint when paired with an async validator.

The pending window now maps to the existing neutral state (`valid: null`, no `data-valid`/`data-invalid`/`aria-invalid`), consistently across modes. The only results kept mid-flight are the ones the form must read synchronously to block submission:

- native constraint failures, published in every mode
- a previously resolved async error in `onChange`/`onBlur` (async results can't block in `onSubmit` mode, per the `validate` docs)

A previously valid result retires in every mode, so no stale success shows for a value that was never validated.

`publish`/`makeValidityData` accept `valid: null` internally; public types already allowed it.

items.title: [field][checkbox][switch] Fix controlled blur validation and stale filled state

labels.name: component: switch
labels.description: Changes related to the switch component.

labels.name: component: checkbox
labels.description: Changes related to the checkbox component.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
Two field lifecycle fixes. The blur half is a regression from #5460; the filled half predates it.

- **Controlled blur normalization no longer discards validation.** With `validationMode="onBlur"`, a blur handler that normalizes the controlled value (e.g. `.trim()`) had its commit retired by the value's prop transition. The blur handler now re-commits the settled DOM value in a microtask, unless it settled back to the initial value (a programmatic reset stays quiet). Async normalization after blur is still not covered.
- **`filled` is now derived from the current value** in a layout effect (the `NumberField` pattern) instead of transition callbacks and write-only mount effects. This fixes stale `data-filled` on remounts and custom `render` elements in `Field.Control`, `Checkbox.Root`, and `Switch.Root`, and `CheckboxGroup` now fully owns the filled state.

`dirty` stays transition-driven: deriving it needs mount-time `initialValue` ordering guarantees and interacts with #5345.
